text:
Maria Chen: FYI I pushed the initial tail analysis from last night's canary. Seeing a recurring surge in decode p99 when qps crosses ~18k. Not obvious hot loop yet.
Jin Park: OK can you drop the profiling summary here? short numbers are fine.
Maria Chen: Sure — aggregated across 6 hosts: prefill p95=42ms p99=89ms, decode p95=120ms p99=480ms (long tails on some requests). Overall p99 for the route ~520ms.
Samir Patel: Whoa decode p99 is massive vs prefill. Is KV cache hit-rate low? That would blow up decode.
Maria Chen: KV hit rate is 87% average but on tail instances drops to ~60% — correlates with longer context/lightweight prompts.
Lia Gomez: Do we have kernel selection logs? maybe the selector picked a slower kernel path for certain seq-len combos.
Jin Park: I dumped the kernel decision trace for two tail samples. Looks like we fell back from fast MMAP kernel to the general path when seq_len>1024 AND kv_miss_count>3.
Oscar Nguyen: That's the change from the selector refactor last week (commit c3f2b9). It was intended to be conservative.
Maria Chen: Here's a minimal log snippet:
```
[trace] req=abcd seq=1300 kv_miss=4 chosen_kernel=general_gemm_v2 ms_decode=310
[trace] req=efgh seq=128 kv_miss=0 chosen_kernel=fast_mmap ms_decode=45
```
Samir Patel: So long sequences + kv misses -> general kernel -> long decode. Two levers: avoid falling back, or reduce kv misses with prefix caching.
Lia Gomez: Also microbatch sizing matters. Larger microbatches increase tail waiting for stragglers. For decode we should be using dynamic microbatch cap at 4 for tail-sensitive routes. Can we lower decode_batch_max at runtime?
Jin Park: We can. Current config for that route is decode_batch_max=12 (throughput-optimized). Dropping to 4 reduces median throughput but improves p99.
Maria Chen: Quick A/B numbers from a local sim: batch_max=12 -> throughput +18% but p99 +2.6x. batch_max=4 -> throughput -9% but p99 drops from 480ms to ~220ms.
Samir Patel: For SLOs we should prioritise p99 SLO over max throughput for this route. Customers hit SLA with tail spikes. Propose default decode_batch_max=6, aggressive kv-prefix caching, and revert that safe-selector rule.
Oscar Nguyen: Reverting selector rule is risky; it was guarding memory/regression cases. Alternative: add fast-path hints when kv_miss_count<=2 OR seq_len<256. That keeps safety but avoids unnecessary fallbacks.
Maria Chen: Good idea. Also we saw that prefill cost is small but prefill+decode combined matters for long completions. Could we pipeline prefill and decode in separate executor pools so prefill doesn't block decode kernels?
Lia Gomez: Yes — split runtimes: prefill runs on batch-optimized pool, decode on low-latency pool with smaller microbatches. Scheduler already supports tagged pools. Need a routing policy change.
Jin Park: I can prototype tagging. Also adding a per-request KV fingerprint to improve prefix cache reuse would raise hit-rate from 87% -> ~93% in sim. That halves kv-miss tail contribution.
perf-bot: perf-regression-detected: commit c3f2b9 increased decode p99 by 1.9x on canary at 1796335000.
Samir Patel: Let's triage: 1) quick revert candidate for selector fallback (hotfix), 2) runtime config change decode_batch_max=6 for affected route, 3) enable prefix cache fingerprinting behind flag, 4) plan pool-split rollout.
Maria Chen: I'll open a follow-up PR with test harness on selector and a patch to config. Assigning @Jin Park for pool split prototype and @Samir Patel for permissioned revert if needed.
Oscar Nguyen: FYI unit tests show no correctness change for selector revert but memory spikes need monitoring. Add a rollback guard in deploy pipeline.
Lia Gomez: For rollout we should gate by p99 telemetry delta <5% and kv hit-rate >85%.
Maria Chen: Timeline: hotfix revert + config change today (canary), finger-print flag staged tomorrow, pool-split next week.
Samir Patel: Sounds good. Any objections? :+1:
Jin Park: +1. I'll start the pool-tagging POC.
Maria Chen: Thanks everyone — will paste PR/links when ready.
Maria Chen: (added) Also adding a quick checklist for the oncall in case tail resurfaces: attach latest kernel traces, kv-miss heatmap, route config dump.
Samir Patel: Nice.
